The expanded health message is bought but not yet shown to have changed the floor: clinic counts are still about a third below a normal Wednesday and the dialysis, MAT and prenatal schedules are the ones still missing. A general 'it is safe to come' line does not speak to the fear that the clinics leak, so it is the reassurance that has already failed to bring people back; until a message says plainly, in household words, what is safe and what is not, those schedules keep shrinking.

Fifteen thousand families still hold the fabricated closure notice as the last word from the division: a correction is promised on the division's own website and the emergency broadcast activation claimed for it has no record of going out, so nothing has landed on a channel that reaches the hollows where the fake arrived. Until one message carrying what is true about closures, clinics and records reaches those phones, the fabricated notice stands.

Public terminals carry guidance on what a genuine division notice looks like, but no verified message about the closures, the clinics or the records has gone out on any channel the fabrication reached; the 15,000 families still hold the fake closure notice as the division's last word, and without a verified correction reaching phones and the hollows the buses and clinics keep answering to a closure that is not happening.

The university's account is public but still stands alone: no second institution the region believes has put its name to it, so the region still has no shared version of yesterday, and any institution that speaks next does so into that vacuum.

The second file of billing and insurance IDs sits on the same paste site with nothing bounding how far the exposure runs: the notification still in draft is written for 31,400 when the two files together describe 47,000, and no ceiling or third-file check has been produced. Aimed work on that ceiling and on a reworked message covering the extra fields, including the fraud guidance the richer data now demands, is what moves this; without it the 15,600 extra people stay unnamed and the scam sites keep holding fields the health system has not confirmed.

A second platform-queue route against the fake 'breach compensation' sites now sits alongside the AG takedown request, and no site has been confirmed down; the transfers that left yesterday are still uncancelled, no household has a routed path to freeze a file, and the library terminals — the only channel the fraud is calling through — still carry no freeze-and-report guidance. Until the terminals carry it, the next call finds the same household with nothing to act on.

The fraudulent 'breach compensation' sites are still reaching households through the county's public terminals, and the terminals still carry no warning against them; nothing has been posted or taken live on the library network, the credit-freeze and fraud clinic remains claimed but not staffed, and the households that already wired money still have no documented route to freeze a file and report. The channel stays open and the same fields keep being collected until a real notice replaces the scam page on those terminals.

A second takedown request for the fraudulent 'breach compensation' sites has been filed and is 20 minutes from taking effect; nothing is confirmed down, the library terminals still carry the scammers' channel rather than the real guidance, and the households who already wired money still have no posted route to freeze a file or report, so the wave keeps collecting.
